---
title: "Validation"
---

## Study design

The validation harness compares cached pipeline flags with Insolvency Service adverse-case
labels. It is cache-only: sampling writes company-number lists, the operator fetches those
lists explicitly, and evaluation then reads cached data. Recent positives are sampled
because older labelled companies are often dissolved, purged, or recovered.

Conditional recall is the share of assessable labelled adverse companies for which the
applicable insolvency signal fires. The denominator excludes records that cannot fairly be
assessed, and every exclusion bucket is reported. Recall is also broken down by case type;
solvent members' voluntary liquidations do not count as adverse cases.

The primary result is the cohort disposition: how many labelled companies the current
pipeline excludes as dissolved/closed, flags, misses, cannot find, or has not fetched. The
positive cohort must be supplied explicitly during evaluation, preventing unrelated entries
in the shared cache from entering the result. Conditional recall applies only to the
currently screenable subset. Since the labels and register usually reflect the same filed
insolvency event, high recall is expected and is not a predictive-performance claim.

The comparison cohort is drawn from active companies in the dated monthly snapshot and
stratified to the positives by SIC section and coarse company-age band. Those are pre-distress
structural confounders; downstream outcomes such as insolvency status, filing compliance, or
charges are never matching dimensions.

## Positive-unlabelled framing

The label publication contains positives, not verified negatives. The control is therefore
unlabelled and merely assumed not to be labelled positive. Its flag rate is not precision and
is not a false-positive rate. The design can measure conditional recall and whether signals
separate from a structurally similar control; it cannot establish accuracy against negative
ground truth or validate the broader concept of trustworthiness.
